analysis:
Examined the head-side Codable code for ProviderMessage and CoordinatorMessage in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Protocol/Messages.swift (lines 649-1708). The PR adds an optional `busy: ProviderBusy?` field to Register and Heartbeat. It is encoded through Self.encodeBusy (lines 1070, 1097) and decoded through Self.decodeBusy (lines 1346, 1372), using the new CodingKeys busy_reason, busy_since_ms and busy_addon (lines 948-951). The encodeBusy/decodeBusy implementations and ProviderBusy are not in the supplied units, so their handling of oversized or untrusted strings is unverified.

Security view: the new fields are provider-to-coordinator advisory status that lets a draining provider be excluded from routing before its first heartbeat. A malicious provider can already withhold service or misreport status (ADV-001, T-007), so a provider-asserted busy flag adds no new trust. The busy field does not carry attestation, authorization or App Attest grant data. It does not touch the encryption path (T-008): the inferenceResponseChunk encoding is unchanged and still emits plaintext `data` only when non-empty. The inferenceError decode still discards the free-form error string. The prefix-cache readyAnchors suffix(16) truncation keeps the deepest anchors, and I saw no security impact there. Receipt authority stays with the coordinator (T-041, SEC-035 unchanged). appAttestResume and appAttestShadow encoding is unchanged.

Remaining integration questions: the coordinator-side Go parser must bound busy_reason and busy_addon lengths and must not trust them for logs or the UI. The encodeBusy/decodeBusy definitions need a check for error handling when the keys are partially present. I found no concrete regression in the supplied excerpts.
